# v0.5.0 — Themes, media gallery, and performance across the board

## Community theme system (Settings → Themes)

Browse, download and apply themes from external git repositories. The
**CSS IS the theme** — a `theme.css` at the repo root sets CSS variables
and adds custom rules (borders, glows, radii, anything); the app resolves
`{{THEME_ROOT}}` placeholders to serve images, fonts and icons from the
theme directory through the asset protocol.

- No git required: downloads are HTTP tarballs through pure-Rust crates
  (`ureq` + `flate2` + `tar`) — works on every platform out of the box
- Update detection: the GitHub API's latest commit SHA is compared with
  the local snapshot; an amber "Update" button re-downloads with one
  click
- Theme size on disk shown on each card; spinner during download
- The built-in Omarchy theme stands down when a community theme is active

### First theme: Tokyo Afterburn

A synthwave neon night over Tokyo (leandroruel/rusty-cleaner-theme-tokyo-afterburn):
magenta afterburn glow, electric blue gridlines, HUD chamfered panels,
thin neon scan ring with glass center, brush-script title, dedicated
sidebar and background art.

## Per-messenger media gallery

Click a messenger (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack, Element)
to browse its media: real thumbnails via the asset protocol, content
sniffing for hash-named blobs without extensions (Discord: 147 files,
WhatsApp: 21 on a real profile). Each tile has a "..." menu — view in
the system viewer, copy to a picked folder, or move there
(cross-volume safe). Select one or all, clean goes to the trash.

## Application icons

The Applications page now shows real app icons — resolved through the
hicolor theme on Linux, DisplayIcon `.ico`/`.png` on Windows — with a
letter fallback.

## Windows: the "never used" column works now

UserAssist records GUI launches by their Start Menu shortcut, not by the
executable; the old matcher compared only exe paths. Matching now also
compares normalized `.lnk` stems and takes the newest timestamp.

## Performance

- Parallel directory walk with a std-only worker pool (5-6x on large
  scans)
- Duplicate detection pre-filters with a 64 KiB head hash before any
  full-file read; hashing and confirmation run on all cores
- Scan progress throttled to 80ms; cleaning shows a determinate progress
  overlay
- Scan completion reveals the result: ring pulse, count-up, button glow

## Other fixes

- Browser/messenger caches are one finding per directory, purged in
  place (never sent to the trash — which could exhaust RAM on Windows)
- Closing browsers fully terminates extension/background processes with
  a 4s grace period; the dialog warns about unsaved work
- Registry fixes require a `.reg` backup and offer System Protection
  (the native Windows applet) as a conscious step — no PowerShell cascade
- WSL scans only the current user's Windows profile, not every account
- Disk metrics prefer the SystemDrive volume on Windows
